question.problem: Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨z,\,x,\,3x+y⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined in Cartesian coordinates as $z=-1$ for $0\le x\le 2$ and $1\le y\le 2.$ Calculate the flux of $F$ through $S$ with respect to the *downward*-pointing unit normal vector $n.$
question.worked_solution:
If $S$ is an oriented surface with unit normal vector $n,$ and $F$ is a continuous vector field, then the flux of $F$ across $S$ measured with respect to $n$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S.
$$

For the surface $z=-1$ for  $0\le x\le 2$ and $1\le y\le 2,$ the downward-pointing unit normal vector is

$$
n=⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩.
$$

Using the fact that $z=-1$ on $S,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F\cdot n & =⟨z,\,x,\,3x+y⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,-1⟩ \\  & =-(3x+y).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can calculate the flux of $F$ across $S$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{S}(-(3x+y))\,\text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-(3x+y))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(-(3x+y))\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{1}^{2}[(\frac{3}{2}{x}^{2}+xy){|}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,]\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{1}^{2}(6+2y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{[6y+{y}^{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$
